headline: Check edge count and reachability
statement: Given n vertices labeled 0 through n-1 and undirected edges, determine whether they form one connected graph without cycles. A single vertex with no edges is a tree.
constraints: No self-loops or repeated undirected edges
intuition: An undirected tree on n vertices has n-1 edges. That count alone is insufficient: a disconnected graph can hide a cycle. After the edge-count check, visit from vertex zero and ensure every vertex is reachable.
approach: Reject unless the number of edges is n-1.
Build an adjacency list in both directions.
Traverse from vertex zero with an explicit stack and a visited set, then compare its size to n.
correctness: A connected undirected graph contains a spanning tree with n-1 edges. If it has exactly that many total edges, no extra edge can create a cycle. Thus edge count plus connectivity is sufficient; both conditions are also necessary for a tree.
bruteForce: Check reachability between every pair of vertices and separately detect cycles; repeated traversals are unnecessary.

complexity.explanation: Each vertex and edge is visited at most a constant number of times; the adjacency list stores both directions.

pitfalls: Edge count alone cannot prove connectivity.
Insert both directions for each edge.
Do not interpret revisiting the parent through an undirected edge as a new vertex.
